messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test case calls ClassUtils.toClass with an Object array containing a null element: new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d }. The expected behavior in the test is to get a Class[] array with String.class, null, and Double.class in the respective positions.

The reported issue (c0.m0(Object[]) throws NPE on null array element) matches what we see in the code of ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]):

- The code first checks if the array itself is null or empty and handles those cases.
- Then it creates a new Class<?> array to store the classes of the input elements.
- It loops through the input array elements and for each element,
  - the code calls array[i].getClass() without checking if array[i] is null.
- This causes a NullPointerException if any element in the input array is null, because calling getClass() on null throws NPE.

This directly causes the test failure, because the test input array has a null element, and the method throws instead of returning an array containing null in the corresponding position.

None of the recent bug reports mention this particular issue with null elements causing NPE in ClassUtils.toClass, so this appears to be a unique bug in this method's handling of null elements.

In summary, the reason for the test failure is that ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]) does not handle null elements gracefully and throws a NullPointerException when encountering them, instead of including null in the output Class array.

Recommended fix would be to add a null check inside the loop in toClass(Object[]) to assign null to classes[i] if array[i] is null, otherwise assign array[i].getClass().

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
